scope: Whole Carboniferous juvenile individual, likely developmental stage3 per2021 paper, not adult and not isolated shell. Anchor YPM IP168040 MazonCreek Moscovian, with same-species published restoration for damaged edges.

scale.note: 2021Results explicit specimen dimensions authoritative. Figure1A caption2mm bar appears inconsistent with approximate width ratio; do not claim ruler and text agree or silently rescale.22.1mm sum is nominal anterior-posterior construction before overlap, not separately measured total.

anatomy: Broad low-domed horseshoe-like prosoma with flattened border, long paired posterolateral genal spines and paired ophthalmic ridges extending backward into spines as same-species Fig1C.
Broad rounded posterior shield with radiating marginal points and expressed shallow segment lines. Use Fig1C edge topology; posterior shield is fused, not a chain of free loose plates.
Straight tapering styliform telson7.9mm. Do not turn into scorpion sting or moderncrab tuckedabdomen.
Under anterior shield: paired small chelicerae, four pairs walkinglegs and a final pair pushinglegs. Jointed limbs kept modest and largely under shell. No antennae, no lobster claws.
Small eyes associated with ophthalmic ridges; no white exposed CNS pattern, no centralbraindecoration.
restoration_boundaries: Actual dorsal YPM IP168040 supplies outline and published dimensions;2021Fig1C is interpreted same-species reconstruction for poorly preserved spine margins, not a second measured specimen.
2020Fig19E-G YPM IP28514 shows real same-species ventral appendages; used only jointed organization, not dimensions or claimed same individual.
CNS nerves indicate chelicera/fourwalking/pushing arrangement in2021discussion; actual ventral fine tips, shellheight, smallmouthparts, stance/color inferred conservatively.
Do not use Limulus juvenile panelE as Euproops fossil, and do not substitute Piesberg Euproops sp adult flange morphology for this juvenile.
